Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0024-reverse-98", "row_sha256": "4a9cbe2a69d964b25a14f0c35087603a9ff6017ca92695b60a07b56445ef1dc9", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, can you put together a clear repair plan for Maple Row Community Library from the meeting notes below? send the finished prompt to Leonie, not Ellis. this is for the library committee to review, not a notice that work has been approved or booked. please keep the actual notes in the prompt so whoever makes the plan can see what we were discussing, and don't turn a guess into a confirmed repair.

meeting was april 16 at 6 pm in the small meeting room at Maple Row. eleven people came: two library staff, five committee members, three regular volunteers, and one person from the city facilities desk. the library is in a city-owned building, but the branch committee handles ordinary repair requests and has to ask the city before work on the outside wall or anything tied to the building's main systems. nobody at the meeting could say whether that city request had been filed. the facilities desk person said they would check the file, not that they would arrange the work.

notes from the walk-through: the north entrance ramp handrail moves a little when pulled, especially at the lower post. the ramp surface is uneven in one place, but nobody measured the change or said it was inaccessible. after heavy rain, water sits near the bottom of the ramp for a while. the drain is on the city side of the walkway, and the meeting did not establish who would clear it. the west entrance has two steps and is not a substitute accessible route. don't describe the ramp as closed; the door and ramp were in use during the meeting. one volunteer said the rail felt “wobbly enough that I wouldn't lean on it.”

inside, there's a brown mark on one ceiling tile in the east reading room, near the window. staff saw it first about three weeks ago. no one checked above the tile, and they don't know if it's old or if there's an active leak. there wasn't water on the floor on april 16. another tile nearby looks intact. the room is used for the weekly story circle on wednesdays at 10:30 and for quiet study the rest of the week. staff can move the circle to the children's tables if needed, but they haven't decided to do that.

boiler notes: staff have heard a short rattling sound from the basement boiler on four evenings since march 28. it stops after a few minutes. the heat has continued to work, and the room temperature readings staff wrote down were 68 to 71 degrees. the sound wasn't heard at the meeting. the service sticker says last inspection october 9, but the notes don't say whether that was a full service visit. the city facilities desk should be asked whether the boiler is on its maintenance schedule; no one has called the service company yet. the plan shouldn't call it broken or say it needs replacement.

there is also an outlet in the workroom that one staff member says sparked once when a label printer was plugged in, on april 11. the printer now uses a different outlet. nobody else saw the spark, the workroom outlet has not been tested, and there has been no report of a smell, heat, or another spark. staff put a small paper note above it saying not to use it for now. the committee did not decide whether that note is enough or whether to call an electrician immediately. don't imply anyone has inspected or cleared it.

money and people: the unrestricted repair reserve currently has $4,800, according to the treasurer's sheet shown at the meeting. a Friends of Maple Row grant might provide up to $1,200, but the application is due June 3 and no award has been made. the grant could only be used for access improvements or safety-related work, according to the notes from last year's call; nobody checked whether that wording is still current. two volunteers can help move chairs and books, but they are not trained to do electrical, boiler, ramp, or ceiling work. staff can handle room signs and tell regular users about a temporary room change. don't assume volunteer labor is free for contractor work or that grant money will be available.

what i need is a practical repair plan that sorts out what to check first, who should be contacted, and what decisions still need to be made. separate the reported conditions from things that still need inspection. show how the ramp, ceiling mark, boiler sound and workroom outlet fit into the plan without claiming a diagnosis. include a sensible order and approximate timing only where the notes support it; if a timing depends on a city response or inspection, say so rather than making up a date. include the reserve and possible grant as separate funding facts, and don't treat the grant as secured. make clear which work would need city coordination and that it's not known whether a request has already been filed.

please make the plan useful to the committee, with a short opening, a numbered section for the repair items or steps, and a final paragraph about coordination and communication. include a note about the wednesday story circle only if a room move becomes relevant; no move has been decided. keep the quote from the volunteer as a quote, and don't turn the west entrance into an accessible alternative. don't write as though repairs, inspections, funding, or approvals have already happened. give the committee a prompt they can use to request the plan, rather than writing the plan itself.", "output": "Prepare a practical repair plan for the Maple Row Community Library committee using the meeting notes below. Address the finished prompt to **Leonie, not Ellis**. The plan is for committee review; it must not suggest that work has been approved or booked. Retain the meeting details and reported conditions so the plan can distinguish observations from matters that still need inspection. Do not present guesses as confirmed repairs or diagnoses.

## Meeting context

The meeting took place on April 16 at 6 pm in Maple Row’s small meeting room. Eleven people attended: two library staff members, five committee members, three regular volunteers, and one person from the city facilities desk. The building is city-owned. The branch committee handles ordinary repair requests, but it must ask the city before work on the outside wall or anything tied to the building’s main systems. It is not known whether a city request has already been filed. The facilities desk representative said they would check the file, not that they would arrange work.

## Reported conditions

1. **North entrance ramp:** The handrail moves a little when pulled, especially at the lower post. One part of the ramp surface is uneven, but no one measured the change or said the ramp was inaccessible. After heavy rain, water sits near the bottom of the ramp for a while. The drain is on the city side of the walkway, and the meeting did not establish who would clear it. The west entrance has two steps and is not an accessible-route substitute. The ramp and door were in use during the meeting; do not describe the ramp as closed. One volunteer said, “wobbly enough that I wouldn't lean on it.”

2. **East reading room ceiling tile:** There is a brown mark on one tile near the window. Staff first noticed it about three weeks before the meeting. No one checked above the tile, so it is not known whether the mark is old or indicates an active leak. There was no water on the floor on April 16, and a nearby tile looks intact. The room is used for the weekly story circle on Wednesdays at 10:30 and for quiet study at other times. Staff could move the circle to the children’s tables if needed, but no move has been decided.

3. **Basement boiler:** Staff have heard a short rattling sound on four evenings since March 28. It stops after a few minutes. The heat has continued to work, and staff recorded room temperatures of 68 to 71 degrees. No sound was heard at the meeting. The service sticker says the last inspection was October 9, but the notes do not establish whether it was a full service visit. The city facilities desk should be asked whether the boiler is on its maintenance schedule. No one has called the service company. Do not call the boiler broken or say it needs replacement.

4. **Workroom outlet:** One staff member reported a single spark when a label printer was plugged in on April 11. The printer now uses another outlet. No one else saw the spark; the outlet has not been tested; and no smell, heat, or further spark has been reported. Staff put a small paper note above it saying not to use it for now. The committee did not decide whether that is sufficient or whether to call an electrician immediately. Do not imply that anyone has inspected or cleared the outlet.

## Funding and available help

The treasurer’s sheet shown at the meeting listed $4,800 in the unrestricted repair reserve. A Friends of Maple Row grant might provide up to $1,200, but its application is due June 3 and no award has been made. Notes from last year’s call say the grant could be used only for access improvements or safety-related work; no one checked whether that wording is still current. Two volunteers can help move chairs and books, but they are not trained for electrical, boiler, ramp, or ceiling work. Staff can put up room signs and tell regular users about a temporary room change. Do not assume volunteer labor is available for contractor work or that grant funding will come through.

## What the plan should cover

Set out what to check first, who should be contacted, and which decisions remain open. Distinguish reported conditions from issues that require inspection. Address all four repair items without claiming a diagnosis. Give a sensible order and approximate timing only where the notes support it; where timing depends on a city response or inspection, say so instead of inventing a date. Present the reserve and possible grant separately, and do not treat the grant as secured. Make clear which work requires city coordination and that it is unknown whether a request has already been filed.

Use a short opening, a numbered section for repair items or steps, and a final paragraph covering coordination and communication. Mention the Wednesday story circle only if a room move becomes relevant, since none has been decided. Keep the volunteer’s statement as a quote, and do not present the west entrance as an accessible alternative. Do not write as though repairs, inspections, funding, or approvals have already happened. Produce a prompt that can be used to request the plan; do not write the repair plan itself."}]
